title: Write unit tests

rubric.description: Tests boundary conditions, invalid inputs, combined conditions
Tests what happens with bad inputs (negative price, unknown user_type, etc.)
Tests are clearly named, follow AAA pattern (Arrange/Act/Assert), grouped logically
Asserts the right values with appropriate precision, not just that something ran

title: Security review
prompt: Review `app.py` in this project for security vulnerabilities. Identify all issues by severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low), explain each clearly, and provide concrete fixes with corrected code examples.

rubric.description: Correctly identifies SQL injection, hardcoded secret, XSS, session issues
Correctly ranks severity (critical/high/medium/low) for each issue
Provides concrete, actionable fixes with corrected code examples
Doesn't miss significant issues; covers all major vulnerability classes present

title: Debug a race condition

rubric.description: Correctly identifies the race condition (non-atomic read-modify-write)
Explains WHY the bug occurs (thread interleaving) in a way a junior dev could understand
Provides a correct fix (threading.Lock, threading.atomic, queue, etc.)
Fix is idiomatic Python, not overcomplicated, handles edge cases

title: Refactor messy code

rubric.description: Names are descriptive, logic is clear, magic numbers/strings are named constants
Refactored code is functionally equivalent — same inputs produce same outputs
Appropriate use of helper functions, constants, type hints, docstrings
Explains what the original code was doing and what was changed, helping the reader learn

title: Architecture decision: caching strategy
prompt: I'm building a REST API that serves user profile data. Each profile fetch requires 3 database queries (user, preferences, activity summary) that together take ~200ms. We have 50k active users, and popular profiles can get 1000 req/min. I need to add caching. What strategy do you recommend and how should I implement it?

rubric.description: Recommends a concrete, appropriate strategy (Redis/Memcached, TTL values, cache key design) with reasoning
Addresses cache invalidation, consistency trade-offs, cold start, memory limits
Provides actionable implementation steps, not just theory
Addresses the 50k users / 1000 req/min scale specifically

title: SQL query optimization
prompt:
This PostgreSQL query is running slowly (3-4 seconds) on a table with 2M orders and 500k users. Optimize it and tell me what indexes to add:

```sql
SELECT u.name, u.email, COUNT(o.id) AS order_count, SUM(o.total) AS total_spent
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = u.id
WHERE u.created_at > '2024-01-01'
  AND o.status = 'completed'
GROUP BY u.id, u.name, u.email
ORDER BY total_spent DESC
LIMIT 100;
```

rubric.description: Identifies the right indexes (composite, partial) with correct column ordering and rationale
Any rewritten query produces identical results to the original
Addresses JOIN semantics issue (LEFT JOIN + WHERE on right table = implicit INNER JOIN), suggests EXPLAIN ANALYZE
Explains why each change helps; mentions query planner behavior

title: Dockerfile production hardening
prompt:
Review this Dockerfile and improve it for production. Point out every issue and provide a corrected version:

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.11
WORKDIR /app
COPY . .
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt
RUN pip install gunicorn
EXPOSE 8000
CMD ["python", "app.py"]
```

rubric.description: Adds non-root user, uses slim/alpine base, avoids running as root
Copies requirements.txt before source, orders layers for cache efficiency
Uses gunicorn/uvicorn properly in CMD, adds HEALTHCHECK, handles signals
Pins base image version, uses .dockerignore concept, cleans up apt/pip cache

title: Accessibility audit
prompt:
Review this HTML form for accessibility issues. List every problem by WCAG criterion, explain the impact on users, and provide corrected HTML: ```html
Name:
Email:
Password must be 8+ characters
I agree to terms
Submit
```

rubric.description: Identifies missing labels (1.3.1), color contrast failure (1.4.3), missing button role (4.1.2), keyboard inaccessibility (2.1.1)
Explains how each issue affects screen reader users, keyboard users, low-vision users
Corrected HTML uses proper <label for>, <button>, aria attributes; fixes contrast
Doesn't miss significant issues; covers all 4+ violations present

title: Rate limiting middleware
prompt: My Express.js API is getting hammered by scrapers. Implement rate limiting middleware with different limits for authenticated vs anonymous users. Anonymous users: 30 req/min. Authenticated users: 300 req/min. Return proper 429 responses with Retry-After headers.

rubric.description: Chooses an appropriate algorithm (sliding window, token bucket, fixed window) with justification
Middleware correctly distinguishes auth vs anon, applies the right limits, handles edge cases
Returns 429 with Retry-After header, RateLimit-* headers per RFC 6585 / draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers
Addresses distributed systems (Redis store), bypass risks, IP spoofing via X-Forwarded-For

title: CI/CD pipeline setup
prompt: Create a GitHub Actions workflow for a Python project that: (1) runs pytest on every PR, (2) lints with flake8, (3) builds a Docker image on merge to main, (4) pushes to GitHub Container Registry (ghcr.io). Make it efficient — don't repeat work unnecessarily.

rubric.description: Workflow syntax is valid, triggers are right (PR for test/lint, push to main for build/push), jobs are properly structured
Uses secrets for GHCR auth, doesn't hardcode credentials, uses least-privilege permissions
Caches pip dependencies, parallelizes test and lint jobs, only builds Docker when tests pass
All 4 requirements implemented; image tagged properly (SHA + latest)
